title: Anime Style Metroidvania - Day 10 (Codex Only)
author: iloseitagain
selftext:
I've been working on a fun little Metroidvania side project using my and my wife's OC characters for about 10 days now.  I shared it with a couple friends as a first look, and they suggested I show others to share some of what Astra can do in a game style that people don't usually make with it.

Everything was done in VS Code with Codex using GPT-6 Astra Max, and sound effects using the ElevenLabs MCP, for the music, one which is a placeholder, and one which was generated in Suno 5 before it released V6 and went bad.  So far a lot of my time has gone into movement, animations and the fights which are obviously the core of a Metroidvania game.

I think this does show that decent 2D animations are entirely possible solely with Astra without using outside help, but it does take some prompting time and iteration to get where you want to go.

None of this was done manually, it's all entirely AI from top to bottom, because I wanted to see how much it could truly do without assistance.  Though I had it build myself a level editor and a few other things that I will need to eventually do manual edits.

Thanks for looking if you do! :)

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: would love some of the promps you uses for the sprite sheets

replies.author: iloseitagain
replies.body:
Sure, I can tell you the basic idea on the initial prompts.

First: I asked it to research Metroidvania style game sprites and gameplay, identify 5 high rated games with different styles in the genre and view at least two gameplay videos and five gameplay screenshots of each.  Create a directory in the shared workspace and place all reference pictures and videos in the directory.  I then prompted it to write a brief to describe visual elements that all five games had in common for: animations, characters, camera angles, graphics, special effects and level design.

Second: I created a separate directory with pictures of our characters that we had over the years.

Third: I told it to create one side view orthographic still view of our characters utilizing visual cues and elements common to all games in the genre as set out in the brief I asked it to create.

Four: I told it to generate one idle animation, one attack animation, and one jump animation in a 4x4 256x256 format, a 4x4 512x512 format and a 4x4 1024x1024 format.  I told it to create a workflow that would allow it to view all of its animation work live, in all 3 formats as a testbed.  Once all 3 initial animations were built, I told it to make all three animations consistent with each other.  For some reason I have found that having it edit smaller sized sprites while comparing against a larger size of the same animation gives the smaller sprites more detail, since it is like generating an additional, more detailed reference it can always see at the same time.

Five: I asked it to interpolate additional frames between each existing frame to smooth out the combat animations until the animation was smooth and indistinguishable from an animation from the initial five references.

Six: Once the three animations were done, I asked it to condense the process we had followed thus far into a workflow to hand off to another agent.  I specified that the agent must create a process so thorough and complete that another agent should be able to recreate these animations from the ground up without ever seeing any game references, the repo itself, or the character references.  The AI created itself production instructions which I told it to reference in [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) for all subsequent animation work.

Seven: Every time I asked it to generate a new animation, I would ask it to refer to the production instructions, and then create "insert animation here"  For example, "create a three hit combo animation, one forward swipe, one lower swipe, and one downward slash."

Eight: Once I had created all of the initial animations, I asked it to open them all in the visual animation testbed and "view the animation, iterate to improve its quality by selecting the three largest problems in the animation and fixing them, then continue to view the animation.  Repeat this ten times for each animation."

After that, all of the animations were mostly done.  I had then told it to follow the same principle in order to create the special effects tied to the animations.

comments.author: Grrossi
comments.body:
Looks great. I think the effects are a bit hard to notice, meaning the hit effect, etc. I didn't even notice they were there at first, but I think the hit effects and damage effects are just too small.

Btw, is Astra on Max effort worth it? I usually use it on medium - extra high. I still have trauma from wasting my 5 hour claude limit in minutes on fable max effort.

replies.author: iloseitagain
replies.body:
The effects definitely need a couple more passes for readability yes!  As for whether Max is worth it, I am one of the people who have the issue some people have been reporting in Codex where Light and Medium actually seem to be using more usage than Max right now.  On another account I used Medium for some website design and it took 22% of my x5 Pro just for some basic work in Three.js.  

For reference, getting to this point in the game took me one week of my Pro x20 sub down to 2%, then I used a reset and it's now at 72%.  So about 1.25x Pro x20 weeks.
